A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSpodFL research, with matching authors, core update equations, and benchmark tasks. The main text, figures, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix V report original Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR10 experiments comparing DSpodFL with decentralized-learning baselines.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix O report original benchmark results, including additional experiments with time-varying resource availability and new accuracy and delay analyses.

M1.justification: The core sporadic SGD and aggregation updates remain unchanged. Algorithm 1, line 13, revises the stated Metropolis-Hastings weight calculation from time-indexed neighbor counts to fixed neighbor counts, which v2 explicitly defines using the graph union.

E1.justification: Fashion-MNIST/SVM and CIFAR10/VGG11 image classification, including IID and non-IID cases, are retained. Appendix O.4 adds a distinct environment with computation and communication availability changing during training; v1's empirical participation probabilities remain fixed.

E2.justification: Corresponding empirical comparisons retain DGD, DFedAvg, Randomized Gossip, and Sporadic SGDs. The additional experiments reuse these comparators; changes to the related-work comparison in Table 1 do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The main experimental settings remain stable. New protocols resample participation probabilities every 1000 iterations, sweep CIFAR10 client counts, and evaluate accuracy by iteration and delay components at specified accuracy targets. Figure 6b changes its stated measurement delay from 5000 to 500, without establishing that the experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained heterogeneity and connectivity sweeps, Appendices O.4-O.6 add temporal-resource robustness tests, accuracy-by-iteration comparisons, and processing-versus-transmission delay decomposition. These analyses substantially extend the examination of whether DSpodFL's advantage comes from iteration efficiency or reduced resource costs. Figure 6c also extends the client-count sensitivity analysis to CIFAR10.

E5.justification: V1 does not describe repeated-run uncertainty reporting. V2 explicitly reports means and one-standard-deviation uncertainty across multiple runs, adding bands and error bars to the main experimental figures. Exact run counts and seeds remain unspecified, so an increase in runs cannot be established.

E6.justification: V2 revises existing plotted results, particularly Figure 2, and adds Figure 6c, Figure 7, and Tables 2-5. Newly reported findings include FMNIST non-IID accuracy of 0.70 for DSpodFL versus 0.75 for DGD at iteration 15000, alongside target-accuracy delay decompositions. These substantially expand the quantitative record without establishing performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: V2 adds general non-convex stationarity analysis under Assumption 4.2, with constant and diminishing learning-rate results and proofs in Appendices G-H and K-L. The earlier PL analysis is retained and revised in Appendices M-N. Theorem 4.11 now treats time-varying probabilities through uniform bounds, and the PL recursion gains the previously omitted alpha-dependent participation residual, changing the resulting gap bound.

C1.justification: V2 broadens its central theoretical contribution from strongly convex and PL-conditioned results to general non-convex convergence guarantees under both learning-rate policies. The abstract and introduction also make heterogeneous, time-varying resource availability a central contribution, while retaining the claim that DSpodFL unifies existing decentralized methods.

C2.justification: V2 revises the learning-rate and participation interpretation of the optimality gap, replacing v1's simple proportionality claims with participation-dependent residuals. Appendix O explains the tradeoff between accuracy per iteration and delay, and decomposes the resource savings. Section 6 acknowledges limited dataset/task validation, although O.5's new assertion that all methods converge to the same global model exceeds the general non-convex stationarity guarantee.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly identifies a cluster of three NVIDIA A100 GPUs with 40 GB memory. This adds reproducibility information absent from v1; it does not establish a hardware change between experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds references on local decentralized SGD, Cooperative SGD, and optimization over directed graphs, while removing several uncoordinated-step-size references. Section 2 sharpens distinctions from the already-cited Anarchic FL and asynchronous framework of Even et al., but retains the central positioning around joint sporadic computation and communication.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and related-work discussion are substantially rewritten. Method exposition is reordered, proofs are consolidated into grouped appendices, and the PL discussion moves out of the main analysis. These are extensive narrative and organizational changes beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column main-text layout with a single-column format, revises Figure 1, expands and restructures Table 1, and adds uncertainty displays. It also adds a third panel to Figure 6, a new Figure 7, and four numerical tables, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens theoretical scope through the additional non-convex analyses and improves precision by correcting the participation-dependent PL residual and gap interpretation. Dynamic-resource experiments, uncertainty reporting, and iteration/delay decomposition provide stronger support for the practical claims. These gains outweigh the overstrong common-global-model assertion in Appendix O.5; exact run counts also remain an unresolved reporting limitation.
